title: Azithromycin as an Adjunct to Corticosteroids in Children With Newly Diagnosed Immune Thrombocytopenia
off: Azithromycin as an Adjunct to Corticosteroids in Children With Newly Diagnosed Immune Thrombocytopenia: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial With Exploratory Analysis of Regulatory T Cells
summary: This study aimed to evaluate the possible immunomodulatory effect of Azithromycin as an adjuvant treatment on the clinical and laboratory outcomes of children with newly diagnosed ITP through its effect on T-reg cells.
desc:
Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by a low platelet count (\< 100 × 109/L) due to enhanced platelet clearance and compromised production, typically manifesting with bleeding.

Azithromycin (AZM), is abroad spectrum macrolide antibiotic with bacteriostatic properties, it also appears to has anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties that are impartial of its antibacterial properties.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Eligible participants were children aged below 12 years.
* Patients with newly diagnosed immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) (within 3 months of onset) who were planned to receive corticosteroids as first-line therapy.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients had any other cytopenia, another autoimmune disease (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus, screened by antinuclear antibody and anti-dsDNA).
* Secondary or suspected inherited thrombocytopenia.
* Congenital anomalies.
* Positive family history of thrombocytopenia, or concurrent severe infection.
* Children who did not respond to first-line therapy and required an additional treatment line.

arms.d: Patients received oral prednisone (2 mg/kg/day, maximum 60 mg, for 5-7 days) plus Azithromycin (AZM) (10 mg/kg/day for 3 days.
Patients received oral prednisone (2 mg/kg/day, maximum 60 mg, for 5-7 days) alone
